description: Delete a sprint of a project's board. Call it with apply=false first (the default): the answer says what deleting would do and changes nothing — the sprint, its state, 'issues' (how many it holds, every project), 'projects' (per project you can open), 'hidden' (the rest, only counted), all of which would go to the backlog. Then call it with apply=true and expectIssues set to that 'issues' number: if the sprint holds another number by then, nothing is deleted (reason count_mismatch) — you looked at another sprint, or it changed. The ACTIVE sprint is not deleted here: complete it with complete_sprint (reason active). A token configured into an agent or a script may delete only an EMPTY sprint; one that holds issues is refused (reason person_needed) — a person deletes it on the board. A deleted sprint goes to the board's TRASH with a record of the issues it held and waits there 30 days — 'inTrashUntil'; until then restore_sprint brings it back with them (list_sprint_trash lists the trash). Its issues — of every project — go back to the backlog, each with a line in its history. Answers 'released', how many issues left it, and 'changeId' — rollback_sprint_change undoes the whole delete in one call. Needs full write access to the project (member, admin or lead); a reporter, a commenter or a read-only member is refused with the reason, as is anybody while the project is paused or archived. Written in the project's journal under your name.

apply.description: false (the default) answers what deleting would do and changes nothing. true deletes — with expectIssues.

expectIssues.description: With apply=true: how many issues the sprint holds, as the preview's 'issues' said. Another number refuses the call.

projectKey.description: Project key whose board holds the sprint, e.g. 'PM'.

sprint.description: The sprint, by name or id from list_sprints. A name is matched exactly; give the id when in doubt.
